correctness.rationale: The proof's hub-selected iff reduces to path zero forcing (endpoint or adjacent selected path pair). With the hub white, no path-to-path force is possible before hub capture, and only an endpoint selected adjacent pair or three consecutive selected path vertices can force the hub. This yields a complete iff forcing criterion. Counting the failed hub-free binary words avoiding initial/final 11 and internal 111 via the four-state transfer matrix gives (1+x)^(m+1)−xQ_m−A_m. For every m>=3, the four minimum sets are two hub/endpoints and two boundary path pairs. Independent brute-force dynamics for each subset at m=3..9 matches the criterion and cardinality counts; those finite tests do not establish the general theorem.
